one_sentence: Miranda-Agrippino and Rey (Review of Economic Studies, 2020) show that a single 'Global Financial Cycle' factor, driven substantially by U.S. monetary policy shocks, governs the comovement of risky asset prices, credit flows and leverage of global financial intermediaries worldwide.

issues.reason: Second author's given name is 'Hélène' Rey; the Web of Science export stripped both accents (é, è). Confirmed against Crossref metadata for DOI 10.1093/restud/rdaa019 and the author's own LBS/helenerey.eu listings.

issues.original: US Monetary Policy and the Global Financial Cycle
issues.corrected: U.S. Monetary Policy and the Global Financial Cycle
issues.reason: The published journal article's title uses 'U.S.' with periods (confirmed via Crossref and Oxford Academic/academic.oup.com landing page for restud/87/6/2754/5834728). The unpunctuated 'US' form matches the 2015 NBER working paper (w21722) title, not the final published version -- a working-paper/published-version title mismatch, not fabrication.

ALL-CAPS with the definite article dropped is the Web of Science journal-abbreviation rendering, not the journal's actual name. The canonical name (Oxford University Press masthead, Crossref container-title) is 'The Review of Economic Studies'.

No DOI field present in the WoS export. Confirmed via Crossref API (api.crossref.org/works/10.1093/restud/rdaa019) and resolves correctly to the Oxford Academic article page. This is the single most load-bearing missing field for a canonical anchor and should be added.

Web of Science internal author-identifier field. Not read by any standard .bst style (plain, apalike, natbib, elsarticle-num, etc.); pure export cruft that should be dropped from a paper's working .bib.

Same category as ResearcherID-Numbers -- a WoS export convenience field with no .bst consumer. (The ORCID number itself, 0000-0002-2214-9063, does check out as Hélène Rey's registered ORCID, so it is not wrong, just not a field any bibliography style will render.)
Web of Science accession number, meaningful only inside the WoS database. No .bst uses it; stray export field.

issues.corrected: (removed, or keep only if the target .bst explicitly supports dual ISSN)
issues.reason: Not a standard BibTeX field consumed by common .bst styles (they read ISSN, not EISSN). The value itself is correct (1467-937X is REStud's registered e-ISSN per Crossref/ISSN Portal) but it is hygiene cruft in the same category as ResearcherID/ORCID/Unique-ID -- harmless if left (silently ignored) but not something any bibliography style will print.
